title: Ring overlay display: anchors only on the selected ring, ring-number toggle, depth-tested lines, constant pixel-size anchors
description:
User review 2026-10-03 of the CRAW-30 ring tool (authored and supporting anchors, drafts); builds on CRAW-30's baseline. The user's 17 saved fertility rings (fixtures/fertility_rings.dsl: ring_candidates plus spline_ring ring_05 to ring_17) must keep drawing correctly.

Make the ring overlay quieter and correct.
1. Anchors only on the selected ring: unselected rings draw as their polyline only; authored and supporting anchor discs appear only on the ring open as the draft.
2. Ring-number labels toggle: a key not already bound in the ring or mesh viewer scenes shows or hides the numbers, listed in the control hints; hidden by default.
3. Hidden behind the model: ring polylines, anchors and labels on the far side of the surface must not show through it. VIEW-11 fixed the depth testing of line passes at its root; route the ring overlay through that same path, with no depth bias.
4. Constant screen-size anchors: anchor discs keep a fixed pixel size at any zoom, so they never grow into each other when zoomed in. Research how Blender and similar editors draw vertices and edges first (Blender's theme vertex size defaults to about 3 px in screen space, drawn as depth-tested points; edges about 1 px) and match that: the supporting anchor is the smallest drawn thing (about 3 px), an authored one a little larger, the selected one larger again. Anchor hit-testing stays in pixels and matches the drawn size.
definition-of-done: 1. Screenshots in tmp/: no anchors on unselected rings; numbers hidden by default and shown after the toggle; the model rotated so rings run behind it with nothing showing through; the same anchors at two zoom levels with the same pixel size. 2. The anchor hit radius matches the drawn size. 3. The Blender findings the sizes are based on are recorded on the ticket. 4. Build checkstyle-green.
testing-plan: 1. F5 on fertility with the saved rings, screenshots per item. 2. Measure an anchor's pixel diameter at two camera distances from the screenshots.
changes-made: CRAW-36 verification (worktree craw-36, launch entry "CRAW-36: ring overlay on fertility rings" = ring-tool scene with -Dixdar.mesh.dsl=fixtures/fertility_rings.dsl, never saved over). 1) Anchors only on the draft: RingTool.uploadOverlay now hands MeshOverlayRuntime.setAnchorDiscs the draft's anchors alone; graph rings, confirmed rings and the hover preview draw as polylines only (tmp/craw36_5_confirmed_ring_no_anchors.png, tmp/craw36_1_numbers_hidden_default.png). 2) Ring numbers: key N (free in ring-tool and mesh viewer; listed in the control hints as "show / hide ring numbers"), RingScene.showRingNumbers, hidden by default (tmp/craw36_1_numbers_hidden_default.png, tmp/craw36_2_numbers_shown_after_N.png, tmp/craw36_2c_numbers_hidden_again.png). Label occlusion now compares eye distances (inverse projection of the depth sample) with a quarter of the label's lift as the tie, replacing the window-depth LABEL_DEPTH_SLACK 0.0005 that spanned ~13 model units at distance 268 and grew with zoom-out. 3) Depth: ring polylines already went through VIEW-11's MeshLineShader; anchors now go through the same rule in new glsl/mesh_anchor.vs/.fs (ShaderType.MeshAnchor, MeshLineShader class): one disc copy per face around the vertex, copies on back faces discard, each fragment takes its face plane's depth at the pixel centre, no bias. Two fixes found while verifying: (a) a grazing face's plane hit runs off far from the line/vertex and lifted far-side pixels through the body (2 stray ring-6 pixels at distance 190, 2 stray supporting-anchor pixels); mesh_line.fs and mesh_anchor.fs now follow a face plane toward the eye at most STEEPEST_FOLLOWED_SLOPE = 4 pixel-widths of depth; (b) ring line groups draw with depthMask(false) so a ring line no longer wins the tie over the anchor disc at the shared vertex. Rotated views: tmp/craw36_4_rotated_behind_az2.4.png, tmp/craw36_4_rotated_behind_az3.9.png. 4) Constant pixel size: discs are screen-space billboards snapped to a pixel centre, diameters supporting 3 px, authored 5 px, selected 7 px (framebuffer pixels). Measured by connected-component count of the exact disc colour: at camera distances 40 (close-up), 190, 268.5 and 600 every supporting anchor is 3x3 (9 px), authored 5x5 (21 px), selected 7x7 (37 px) (tmp/craw36_3_draft_anchors_d40_closeup.png, _d190.png, _d268.5.png, _d600.png). Hit test: RingTool now hit-tests authored anchors in pixels against the drawn disc (radius = diameter/2 around the same snapped pixel centre, plus an occlusion check) instead of ANCHOR_HIT_PIXELS 12 in world units; a hover sweep over the 9x9 pixels round one authored anchor gave 21 hit pixels = 21 drawn pixels, 0 mismatches (tmp/hit_vs_drawn.txt). Blender findings (manual and Python API docs only, no source): Preferences > Themes > 3D Viewport carries Vertex Size, Edge Width and Face Dot Size as pixel values; bpy ThemeView3D documents vertex_size range 1-10, edge_width 1-32, facedot_size 1-10, and object_origin_size "Diameter in pixels" 4-10; Blender Artists threads confirm vertices keep the same size when zooming. The default theme values themselves (vertex 3 px, edge 1 px, face dot 4 px as commonly cited) could NOT be confirmed from documentation: the API page lists RNA default 0 and the manual's theme page gives no numbers; the defaults live only in Blender's GPL source, which is banned. Sources: https://docs.blender.org/api/current/bpy.types.ThemeView3D.html, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/editors/preferences/themes.html, https://blenderartists.org/t/increase-size-of-vertices/379157. Build: mvn -q compile green (checkstyle included); mvn test 340 run, 0 failures. Not fixed (pre-existing VIEW-11 behaviour, out of scope): zoomed in to distance 40 the draft spline's straight chords dip under the curved surface and short stretches of the pink line are hidden; same with the slope clamp disabled.

User review 2026-10-03: authored anchors were too hard to click at a 2.5 px radius. Anchors keep their drawn sizes (3/5/7 px), but the click radius is now max(drawn radius, ANCHOR_HIT_RADIUS_PIXELS = 8) in RingTool. This replaces DoD item 2 (hit radius matches drawn size) by user decision.
